Laredo will host its annual H-E-B Feast of Sharing on Wednesday, November 4, from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. at the Sames Auto Arena, 6700 Arena Blvd., according to the Laredo Morning Times and H-E-B's event calendar.

The free holiday dinner is open to the public, no ticket or reservation required, and brings together family, friends and neighbors for food, music and good cheer, according to H-E-B.

The Feast of Sharing is a series of festive gatherings that serve more than 340,000 meals at 34 dinners throughout Texas and Mexico, according to H-E-B. Laredo holds a special place in that history: H-E-B launched the tradition in 1989 with dinners in Corpus Christi and Laredo, and the Laredo dinner is now in its 38th year.

The event is part of H-E-B's Hunger Relief Program, which works year-round to prevent hunger. Last year, the program donated 34 million pounds of food to families in need, and since 1982 it has donated more than 1 billion pounds of food to 5,500 nonprofit organizations in Texas and Mexico, according to H-E-B.

For Laredo families, the timing matters: the dinner lands the day after Election Day, in the first week of November, as the holiday season gets underway — and it is free to everyone who walks in.

Why it matters

A free, open-to-everyone holiday meal in a city where food insecurity is a year-round concern is more than a photo opportunity. It is also a reminder of where the tradition started: Laredo was there at the very first Feast of Sharing, and 38 years later the table is still open.
